title: Kent Beck's SUnit and the xUnit Lineage Behind pytest and Jest
explainer: The fixture/assert vocabulary this lesson teaches traces back to SUnit, a testing framework Kent Beck described for Smalltalk in a 1989 paper. Beck later ported the design to Java with Erich Gamma as JUnit, and the isolated-test-case, setup/teardown-around-each-test pattern spread from there into what's now informally called the "xUnit" family - Jest's beforeEach/afterEach genuinely descends from it (via Jasmine, which is explicitly xUnit-style). Pytest is the interesting exception: its fixture system was a deliberate departure from xUnit-style setUp/tearDown, built instead around dependency-injected functions - proof that even a widely-copied design pattern isn't the only way to solve the same problem.
